newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson might move head office abroad - report.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson might move head office abroad - report.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson will decide before this summer whether it will move its head office abroad, daily Dagens Industri reported on Monday.
"Before the summer... an investigation will be ready," Ericsson spokesman Lars Stalberg told the newspaper.
Ericsson Chief Executive Lars Ramqvist said in a radio interview at the weekend that the company board had decided to look into a possible move of the Stockholm head office because of tax reasons.
"For tax reasons it is almost hopeless to get a foreigner to move here," Ramqvist told the radio.
"If politicians don't understand that we must reward development and competence, Ericsson won't manage the restructuring we are facing," Ramqvist said.
"If our development people would rather move to the U.S. or England, what will we do then?"
Junior Finance Minister Thomas Ostros said the government is looking into new tax rules for key foreign staffers.
"If they only stay a few years they don't have the same need for the services our taxes are financing," he was quoted by daily Dagens Nyheter as saying.
Neighbouring Finland has special tax rules for foreigners.

A foreign boss who earns more than 35,000 Finnish markka a month pays a maximum of 35 percent in tax, while the corresponding tax rate for a Finnish boss with the same salary is 70 percent, Dagens Nyheter said.
